_note: How a part's condition (0–100, on the owned part) scales what it does, by the part's category: each curve is [condition, factor] points (straight lines between), and the factor multiplies the target in the physics spec, applied after the modifiers. Condition 100 is always a factor of 1: a part in perfect condition is exactly as defined. A category with no entry doesn't wear (body panels, wheels). Tyres on several corners use their average condition. A curve with per: "part" goes by each part's own condition instead (a crumpled bumper, whatever the doors are like): each worn part's value, multiplied together, or with op: "add" added to the target (slots: only parts in those slots).

engine._note: power loss: compression, worn rings and valves

tyres._note: grip loss: worn tread, hardened rubber

brakes._note: worn pads and glazed discs start to fade at a lower temperature, and fade fully sooner

body._note: crumpled panels: each adds a little drag
a smashed front lets air under and into it: more lift

aero._note: a broken wing or spoiler drags
